verdict: Caution: lend selectively to API units with US FDA-cleared plants, diversified customers and tight working capital; avoid single-customer, single-product units with stretched receivables.
title: Patancheru API / bulk drugs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**An API unit is a reactor-and-solvent factory: it buys solvents, intermediates and catalysts, runs multi-step chemistry in pressure reactors, and sells certified bulk powder to formulators.** Cash is made on yield, solvent recovery and reactor occupancy, not on price. Pricing power is thin because the buyer is a regulated formulator who can switch on a failed audit; the real moat is a clean regulatory file. So when a proposal lands, check the plant's approval status first; if the unit cannot show a current US FDA or equivalent clearance, ask which customers it actually ships to. [1][2]

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Working capital is the business: long inventory and long receivables tie up cash for months.** A rating report on an API maker put the working-capital cycle at around 185 days, driven by high raw-material inventory holding [9]. That is the number to underwrite, not the sales line. The data pack shows India-wide output at -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY, a gap of +23.7 pp [D] — so credit is running well ahead of real output, and we should not let a borrower's growth story substitute for volume evidence. Telangana itself is running hot: GST +13.8% and electricity demand +15.7% Apr-to-date, both faster than India [D].

## The growth opportunity in Patancheru
**Pursue the second-tier API and CDMO units riding the peer upcycle, not the commodity fermenters.** Peer results are strong: Aarti Pharmalabs posted record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][5]; Akums cited improved API prices and CDMO volume gains [6]; RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth [7]. Local hiring at Arene Lifesciences across production, QA, QC and regulatory affairs signals real capacity running in Pashamylaram [1], and Aurobindo's Telangana arm received a US FDA EIR in March 2026 [2] — note that source is eight months old. **Target units with an EIR, more than one regulated customer, and CDMO or custom-synthesis work.** Avoid single-product, single-customer units selling into unregulated markets.

## How to grow safely
**Structure for the working-capital cycle, not the P&L.** Size the limit to the 185-day cycle [9], take monthly stock-and-debtor statements, and covenant a maximum working-capital cycle and a gearing ceiling; a rating note flags gearing above 2 times as a downward trigger [8]. Take monthly GST returns and quarterly reactor-utilisation data. If receivables stretch beyond the stated cycle, ask for the ageing by customer before any enhancement.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the regulatory file and the customer list, because both break before the balance sheet does.** A failed audit or a lost ANDA customer shows up as a demand drop first. If a borrower's top customer crosses a third of sales, ask for the contract. If solvent or intermediate costs spike and price cannot pass through, margin compresses fast. Collect from customer the actual inventory-holding and receivable days — the 185-day figure is an old rating reference, not this borrower's.

## The call
**Caution, not avoidance.** Telangana's local demand is genuinely strong [D], but the credit-versus-output gap [D] and the long cash cycle [9] mean we lend to proven, audit-clean units and decline the rest. Sources say little specific to Patancheru's own credit behaviour, so lean on first principles and the peer set above.
watch: Filing gap or falling turnover vs stock statements -> freeze limit enhancement and inspect godown
Top customer above one-third of sales -> demand contract and diversify covenant
US FDA warning letter or import alert -> stop fresh disbursement, review account
Utilisation below stated plan for two months -> ask for order book and reprice risk
Gearing above 2 times [8] -> no new capex funding, seek promoter infusion
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local demand strong but credit far outpacing output; peer API results positive.
